page.heroLead: Discover a new kind of complementary treat made with dried black soldier fly larvae. A different way to bring variety to feeding time for your pets.
page.heroFine: In development for the Paraguayan market. Availability and permitted species are subject to the relevant approvals.

page.productDescription: A practical dried insect-protein format, developed as a complementary treat rather than a complete food. Intended to add variety where appropriate for the species and its diet.
page.spec3v: Complementary feed; follow the approved label
page.productFine: Final pack format, composition, feeding directions and price will be confirmed before sale.
page.whyLead: The black soldier fly is an insect studied as an alternative protein source for animal nutrition. We see its potential both as an ingredient and as part of a more circular system.
page.feature1d: BSF larvae contain protein and fats. Composition varies with feed and processing; the final product analysis will be provided on the label.
page.feature2d: Drying makes larvae easier to handle than fresh larvae. Our treat format is designed for convenient storage according to the label.
page.feature3d: Treats provide variety, but do not replace a balanced diet. Use only for listed species and follow the feeding directions.
page.storyP1: At InnovaProtein, we are developing a way to connect the recovery of organic resources with animal nutrition. Our vision is to turn permitted, traceable raw materials into useful ingredients through insect rearing.
page.storyP2: We will begin with dried larvae from specialist suppliers. As we validate quality, demand and regulatory requirements, we aim to develop our own production in Paraguay.
page.storyP3: Local circular production is a development goal, not a claim about the origin of the launch product.
page.step1d: Begin with qualified suppliers of larvae for animal nutrition.
page.step2d: Confirm quality, traceability, product acceptance and sales requirements.
page.step3d: Develop insect rearing in Paraguay using only permitted, controlled substrates.
page.retailHeading: A new category for your store.
page.retailLead: We want to connect with pet shops, specialist retailers and distributors interested in insect-based treats. Help us understand the right format, your market needs and distribution requirements.
page.retailRightDesc: Ask about availability, future samples, product specifications and distribution opportunities.
page.faq1: What is the black soldier fly?
page.faq1a: Hermetia illucens is an insect species whose larvae are used as an alternative nutrient source in animal nutrition applications. InnovaProtein is developing a whole dried-larvae product.
page.faq2: Which pets will it be suitable for?
page.faq2a: Suitable species, ages and feeding quantities will be identified on the final label following assessment and the relevant approvals. Do not feed to an unlisted species; consult a veterinarian if unsure.
page.faq3a: No. The product is intended as a treat or complementary feed, not a substitute for a complete and balanced diet.
page.faq4a: The launch is based on sourcing from specialist suppliers. Our longer-term goal is to develop local production in Paraguay using permitted substrates and controlled procedures.
page.faq5a: We are preparing the launch and have not announced a retail price or launch date. We will share stockists and final label information once confirmed.
page.faq6: How should I store and feed it?
page.faq6a: Follow the storage directions, expiry date and feeding guide on the final package. Do not use products with damaged packaging or signs of spoilage.

launchIntro: For launch, InnovaProtein plans to buy already-dried larvae. Follow the ingredient from supplier delivery to a prospective retailer.
futureIntro: Paraguayan rearing and drying could eventually supply the same checks, packing and distribution steps. Explore what would change upstream.
source: Specialist animal-nutrition suppliers would provide whole black soldier fly larvae already dried. The supplier lot would travel with the ingredient into the receiving check.
checks: At the bench, the receiving team would match the lot to its source records and check it against the planned specifications before packing.
A lot linked to its checks
pack: Whole dried larvae would be portioned, sealed and linked to their lot. The model uses the proposed package artwork. Final labeling and feeding directions would be confirmed before sale.
retail: Packed cases would move through a distributor to pet shops and specialist retailers in Paraguay. The truck illustrates a proposed delivery route.
A delivery to a retail partner
rear: In a future Paraguayan operation, larvae could grow in trays on permitted, traceable inputs. The enlarged tray shows the live larvae that would precede harvesting.
dry: After harvest, a future local drying step would prepare the whole larvae for storage and batch checks. The cabinet illustrates a process that still needs validation.
